hero.title: Organic-Inorganic Energy Storage Materials Laboratory
hero.subtitle: Energy Storage Materials Development
hero.description: The laboratory develops organic and inorganic energy-storage materials through synthesis, tuning, characterization, and electrochemical analysis.

lab.name: Organic-Inorganic Energy Storage Materials Laboratory
lab.fullName: Organic-Inorganic Energy Storage Materials Laboratory, Department of Chemistry, Providence University
lab.description: The laboratory develops organic-inorganic energy-storage materials spanning polymers, metal oxides, high-entropy materials, metal sulfides, hydroxides, and sustainable biomass materials. Research integrates synthesis and thermal tuning with structural, morphological, elemental, synchrotron, operando, and electrochemical analysis to reveal storage mechanisms.

director.name: Feng-Hao Hsu
director.title: Assistant Professor / PI
director.education: Ph.D., Department of Materials Science and Engineering, National Chung Hsing University
director.bio: Focuses on composition, interfaces, and electrochemical mechanisms in organic-inorganic energy-storage materials, using operando spectroscopy and structural analysis to connect material properties with storage performance.

features.title: Synthesis
features.description: Establish controlled precursor and growth routes for targeted material compositions and morphologies.

features.title: Material Tuning
features.description: Use thermal treatment and atmosphere control to tune crystallinity, defects, and surface chemistry.

features.title: Structural Identification
features.description: Build complete structural information from crystal phase and functional groups to local chemical environments.

features.title: Morphology Analysis
features.description: Examine dimensions, microstructures, and surface features to connect morphology with electrochemical behavior.

features.title: Physical Property Analysis
features.description: Measure thermal behavior, pore structure, and dispersion to assess material stability and transport potential.

features.title: Elemental Qualitative and Quantitative Analysis
features.description: Determine surface and bulk composition, oxidation states, and elemental concentrations for traceable formulations.

features.title: Synchrotron Radiation Techniques
features.description: Use high-brightness X-rays to probe atomic-scale structure and electronic states for reaction-mechanism insight.

features.title: Electrochemical Experiments
features.description: Evaluate storage reactions, kinetics, and cycling stability across multiple scales, including operando analysis.

researchDirections.title: Polymers
researchDirections.description: Explore conducting polymers and polymer composites for batteries, supercapacitors, and flexible energy-storage devices.

researchDirections.title: Metal Oxides
researchDirections.description: Engineer nanostructured metal oxides to improve surface area, redox activity, ion transport, and supercapacitor performance.

researchDirections.title: High-Entropy Materials
researchDirections.description: Use multi-element synergy to design high-entropy materials with stable structures, active sites, and efficient storage kinetics.

researchDirections.title: Metal Sulfides
researchDirections.description: Develop high-capacity, high-rate electrochemical electrodes using the compositionally diverse and redox-active properties of metal sulfides.

researchDirections.title: Energy-Storage Hydroxides
researchDirections.description: Optimize layered hydroxides and composite structures for ion diffusion and charge transfer in high-performance energy-storage systems.

researchDirections.title: Sustainable Biomass Materials
researchDirections.description: Transform biomass resources into functional carbons and composites for circular, low-carbon, and electrochemical energy-storage applications.
